title: How a switch runs its cases
request: Teach me how a switch statement with a missing break falls through, as a still, a narrated video and an interactive video.

diagnostics.gcc-16:
fallthrough.c: In function 'main':
fallthrough.c:7:9: warning: this statement may fall through [-Wimplicit-fallthrough=]
    7 |         puts("one");
      |         ^~~~~~~~~~~
fallthrough.c:8:5: note: here
    8 |     case 2:
      |     ^~~~
fallthrough.c:9:9: warning: this statement may fall through [-Wimplicit-fallthrough=]
    9 |         puts("two");
      |         ^~~~~~~~~~~
fallthrough.c:10:5: note: here
   10 |     case 3:
      |     ^~~~

claims.text: The program sets n to 2 and switches on n. Case 2 has no break.
claims.justification: Read directly from programs/fallthrough.c: line 4 is int n = 2; line 5 is switch (n); lines 8-9 hold case 2 and puts("two") with no break before case 3 on line 10.

claims.text: A switch jumps to the case label whose value matches the controlling expression.
claims.justification: C17 6.8.4.2p5: if a converted case value matches the promoted controlling expression, control jumps to the statement following the matched case label. Here n is 2, so control jumps to case 2.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: If a converted value matches that of the promoted controlling expression, control jumps to the statement following the matched case label.

claims.text: A case label is only a label. It does not stop execution.
claims.justification: C17 6.8.1p4: labels in themselves do not alter the flow of control, which continues unimpeded across them. case 3: is a label, so control flows past it into puts("three").

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: Labels in themselves do not alter the flow of control, which continues unimpeded across them.

claims.text: With n = 2, the switch runs case 2 and then falls through into case 3, so it prints two, then three.
claims.justification: Combines c.match (enter at case 2) and c.labels (case 3: does not stop control). The captured run of programs/fallthrough.c prints two on line 1 and three on line 2.

claims.text: A break statement ends the smallest enclosing switch or loop. Here that is the switch, so execution continues after it.
claims.justification: C17 6.8.6.3p2: a break statement terminates execution of the smallest enclosing switch or iteration statement. The break on line 12 is not inside any loop, so it ends the switch and control continues at line 16; case 4 never runs.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: A break statement terminates execution of the smallest enclosing switch or iteration statement.

claims.text: After the switch ends, the program prints done.
claims.justification: puts("done") on line 16 follows the switch; the captured run prints done on line 3.

claims.text: With n = 2, with_break.c prints only two from the switch, and then done.
claims.justification: programs/with_break.c: n = 2 jumps to case 2 (line 9), puts("two") runs, and the break on line 11 ends the switch (C17 6.8.6.3p2); puts("done") on line 18 runs next. The captured run prints two then done.

claims.text: Which answer do you predict? Pick one of the four. Then the answer plays.
claims.justification: Retrieval prompt required by the learner workspace's predict-first contract; it invites the learner to commit to one of the question's options before the answer is shown, and states no fact about C.

sources.title: Learner workspace contract (AGENTS.md: ask one bounded prediction, wait for the attempt)

claims.text: A case label only marks where execution enters a switch; it never ends a case. In fallthrough.c, the break on line 12 is what ends the switch.
claims.justification: Entry: 6.8.4.2p5 (control jumps to the statement after the matched label). Labels do not alter control flow: 6.8.1p4. The break on line 12 of programs/fallthrough.c ends the switch: 6.8.6.3p2. The sentence does not claim break is the only way out (return, goto and others also leave); it names what ends this switch.

claims.text: If no case label matches and the switch has no default label, no part of the switch body runs.
claims.justification: C17 6.8.4.2p5, last sentence: if no converted case constant expression matches and there is no default label, no part of the switch body is executed. programs/fallthrough.c and programs/with_break.c have case labels 1 to 4 and no default, so any other value of n skips the body and control continues after the switch.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: If no converted case constant expression matches and there is no default label, no part of the switch body is executed.

claims.text: If execution reaches the end of the switch body without a break, the switch ends there.
claims.justification: The switch body is the statement that the switch jumps to, into or past (C17 6.8.4.2p4). Inside it, statements execute in sequence unless a jump such as break changes that (6.8p2). In both programs case 4 is the last labelled statement and has no break, so after puts("four") the body has no statements left, the switch statement completes, and execution continues with the next statement, puts("done") (line 16 of fallthrough.c, line 17 of with_break.c).

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: Except as indicated, statements are executed in sequence.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: A switch statement causes control to jump to, into, or past the statement that is the switch body, depending on the value of a controlling expression, and on the presence of a default label and the values of any case labels on or in the switch body.

claims.text: with_break.c adds a break after case 1 and after case 2, so no case runs on into the next case.
claims.justification: Compared with programs/fallthrough.c, programs/with_break.c adds break; on line 8 (after case 1) and line 11 (after case 2). Case 3 already ends with break (line 14) and case 4 is the last case, whose statements end at the closing brace of the switch body (line 17), so no case's statements are followed by another case's statements. gcc-16 with -Wextra (which enables -Wimplicit-fallthrough) reports nothing for with_break.c, while it warns twice for fallthrough.c.

claims.text: gcc warns about a case that can run on into the next one when -Wimplicit-fallthrough is on, as it is under -Wextra.
claims.justification: GCC documents -Wimplicit-fallthrough (warn when a switch case falls through) and enables -Wimplicit-fallthrough=3 with -Wextra. The capture compiles every program with gcc-16 -Wall -Wextra and records its diagnostics: fallthrough.c gets 'this statement may fall through' at lines 7 and 9.

misconceptions.statement: Execution stops at the next case label, so the program prints only two and done.
A switch runs every case from the top, so the program prints one, two, three and done.
Fallthrough keeps going to the last case, giving two, three, four and done.

trace.label: n is 2: the switch looks for case 2
No break: falls into case 3, prints three
break ends the switch: prints done
with_break.c: a break after every case that runs
